review.title: WebPlayerAdapter: the existing Shaka path, behind the boundary
review.acceptance: The Shaka path that exists today satisfies PlayerAdapter without being rewritten. ADOPT, WRAP, ADAPT: PlaybackController, <liberty-video>, the XState machine and the failure classifier are working, reviewed code and are wrapped, not replaced. REQUIRED: canPlay answers for a DRM candidate with a reason on the accepting branch too, because this adapter is the DRM path on BOTH targets and 'it can play it' must be as legible as a refusal. REQUIRED: getTracks reports text and audio tracks from the Shaka player, which is the first time this repository reads them at all. REQUIRED: dispose is idempotent and releases the CDM session, a hazard three separate comments in the existing player already name. REQUIRED: no behaviour change observable at the existing e2e boundary -- the critical-journey and playback-session suites must pass unchanged, and that is the evidence that this was a wrap rather than a rewrite.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on a3e1d6e. cd apps/web && npx vitest run src/components/player/web-player-adapter.test.ts -> 20 tests passed, exit 0 (re-run at 04:33 as the record for this gate); monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 packages with apps/web at 1026 tests, exit 0. WHAT THE 20 TESTS ASSERT. canPlay DELEGATES AND load RE-ASKS: the adapter never re-derives a protection reading of its own -- it calls protectionDecisionFor, and load() calls the SAME canPlay before touching the media element, so routing cannot be bypassed by calling load directly. A protected candidate is accepted only because WebShakaCapabilities declares a CDM; an unknown-protection candidate is accepted on the same branch, which is the state !== "clear" rule inherited from the contract rather than restated here. TRACK READING IS THE FIRST IN THE REPO: Shaka variants are collapsed to one audio row per language, asserted against a fixture with three variants sharing two languages. AV-SYNC TELEMETRY IS HONEST: readAvSyncTelemetry returns { available: false, why: "adapter_cannot_observe" } rather than a fabricated number, asserted directly. DISPOSE IS IDEMPOTENT: called twice it removes every media listener exactly once, and it completes even when a subscriber throws (asserted with a throwing subscriber and a post-condition on the listener set). MediaElementLike is structural, so the suite runs with no DOM and no Shaka runtime.

review.title: Capability routing decides the engine before playback, with a reason on both branches
review.acceptance: Which engine plays a candidate is decided before playback and recorded with a reason, satisfying the architecture invariant that already states this. REQUIRED: the routing function is PURE and deterministic -- no clocks, no I/O, no ambient state -- on the same rule ADR-003 and ADR-005 apply to ranking, so a routing decision can be reconstructed from a bug report. REQUIRED: a candidate whose contentProtection requires a CDM routes to the web adapter, always, and the native adapter REFUSES it with drm_required_no_cdm rather than falling back or degrading. mpv has no CDM; a native path that tried would be the DRM circumvention CONTENT_RIGHTS.md forbids, so this refusal is a rights property and not a capability detail -- which is why this task carries a rights-review gate. REQUIRED: the reason is recorded on the accepting branch as well, so 'why is this playing natively' is answerable. REQUIRED: routing consumes the protection state already on the session contract (PL-0902) rather than re-deriving it, because two opinions about a candidate's protection would eventually disagree. THE CANDIDATE-PROJECTION FINDING FROM PW-0201 IS THIS TASK'S, per gpt-architect's round-81 ruling, and no separate follow-up is filed unless this task proves one is needed. PW-0201 could not implement `canPlay(candidate: PlaybackCandidate)` as docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md §3 writes it: that client type is `{ id, providerId, source }`, it predates PL-0902, and it carries neither `protection` nor `compatibility` -- so an adapter handed one is STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of returning `drm_required_no_cdm`, which is the refusal this task exists to make. The boundary therefore declares a narrow adapter-facing projection, and that projection is ACCEPTED. REQUIRED HERE: routing consumes the protection state from the playback-session CONTRACT -- the `protection` field `playbackSessionCandidateSchema` already publishes, which PL-0902 put there -- and never re-derives it; the adapter capability input is that narrow projection and nothing wider; NO SECOND DRM OR PROTECTION DECISION IS INVENTED anywhere in the routing path, because two opinions about a candidate's protection would eventually disagree and the reason trail would then explain a decision nobody made; and the native refusal `drm_required_no_cdm` remains STRUCTURAL rather than conditional. DO NOT change the adapter back to the older type to match the §3 prose: the prose was written on 2026-09-15 and PL-0902 landed after it, so the listing is stale and the code is right. A cross-package contract change is only to be proposed if this task PROVES one is required, with the specific field and the specific decision that cannot be made without it.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on a3e1d6e. npx vitest run src/components/player/adapter-routing.test.ts -> 15 tests, exit 0; monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 with apps/web at 1026 tests, exit 0. THE DRM CLAUSES ARE ASSERTED AS RIGHTS PROPERTIES, NOT CAPABILITY ONES. "NEVER DEGRADES" IS A PROPERTY TEST, not an example: fast-check generates arbitrary candidates -- arbitrary id, providerId, URL, mimeType and compatibility -- crossed with three protected states, 300 runs, and requires the native decision to be playable === false in every one. No field on a candidate can turn the refusal off, because a fallback from native to web on decrypt failure would be a system that keeps trying until something plays -- the shape docs/CONTENT_RIGHTS.md forbids as fallback logic whose purpose is to evade provider enforcement. UNKNOWN PROTECTION IS REFUSED TOO, as its own test: requiresContentDecryptionModule is written state !== "clear" so that anything which is not a positive assertion of clearness needs a CDM, and the opposite reading is the invariant-2 incident DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 4 names. A PROTECTED CANDIDATE REACHES SHAKA BY THE NATIVE ENGINE REFUSING IT, asserted by requiring both decisions in the outcome with the refusal first, rather than by reordering the preference list -- so the refusal is IN THE TRAIL. NO SECOND OPINION: a source assertion requires the module to contain no local state === "protected" or state !== "clear" test. NO LICENCE URL IN A REASON: the fixture's licence URL carries a token and the trail is asserted to contain neither it nor the host. PURITY IS ASSERTED TWO WAYS: identical routing twice, and the source may not contain Date., Math.random, process.env, fetch( or globalThis, with a non-vacuity check.

review.title: Profiles become usable: a picker, a switch, and a create
review.acceptance: A person can see who they are watching as, switch, and create a profile. THE BACKEND IS COMPLETE AND REVIEWED AND NOTHING RENDERS IT: /api/v1/profiles and /api/v1/profiles/selection exist with handlers, contracts and tests, and there is no picker, no switch, no create and no avatar anywhere in the application. REQUIRED: the active profile is visible in the shell at all times, because every progress and watchlist row in this product is profile-scoped and a viewer who cannot see which profile is active cannot understand their own continue-watching list. REQUIRED: profile selection goes through the existing selection route and the existing ProfileScope, never through a client-held id -- PL-0405 recorded a forgeable-scope defect and this UI must not reintroduce it, which is why a security review is required. REQUIRED: switching profiles invalidates any cached profile-scoped view rather than leaving another profile's rows on screen.

typecheck.evidence: EXECUTED on ead34dc. npm run typecheck at the root, own invocation, turbo 21/21, exit 0. Also npm run lint 11/11 with zero problems and zero warnings, and npx turbo run build --force 11/11 with apps/web compiled successfully -- the build is not a required gate here but a new route that does not build is not a route, and /profiles appears in the emitted route manifest as a dynamic (server-rendered on demand) entry, which is what export const dynamic = force-dynamic asks for. THREE LINT FINDINGS WERE FIXED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED, and one of them was a real defect: react-hooks/set-state-in-effect flagged the picker's initial load, and the fix was not a disable comment but rewriting the effect as an async closure with a live flag -- the component previously had no unmount guard at all, so a viewer who navigated away before the list resolved would have had setState called on an unmounted component. The other two were an unescaped apostrophe in the heading and an unused catch binding, the latter now an intentional bare catch whose comment states that the parse error is discarded because it quotes the offending bytes.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on ead34dc. cd apps/web && npx vitest run over the three new suites -> avatar 15, profiles-client 20, profile-ui 14, exit 0; monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 packages, exit 0, with apps/web at 63 files / 1075 tests, up from 1026 last round, and every other package unchanged. WHAT THE 49 TESTS ARE FOR, BY THE PROPERTY THEY DEFEND. NO CLIENT-HELD SCOPE, WHICH IS THE SECURITY CORE: listProfiles is asserted to send no body, no query and no id, and the URL is asserted not to contain a question mark -- PL-0405 recorded a forgeable-scope defect and a ?profileId= on a read is exactly how it comes back. selectProfile is asserted to be the only function that sends an id, to send it in the body of the selection route and never in the path or a query, and to pass a malformed id straight through rather than pre-judging it, because isMintedProfileId is the single authority and a second pattern here would answer request_malformed where the first answers profile_unavailable -- itself a small oracle. A source scan over all three modules asserts none of them reads localStorage, sessionStorage, document.cookie, useSearchParams, URLSearchParams or window.location, so there is no client-side source of a profile id anywhere in the directory. NOTHING UNEXPECTED REACHES THE DOM: four tests cover the unreadable path, including that an HTML error page, a script tag and a token-bearing JSON body all produce a detail containing none of their bytes -- only the zod issue PATHS and the HTTP status. A REFUSAL IS AN ANSWER, NOT A FAILURE: a 403 refused body and a 503 unavailable body both classify as answered with their reason trail intact, because collapsing them would throw away the only thing the viewer or support can act on. THE ORDER IS THE SERVER'S: three profiles served in a deliberately non-alphabetical, non-chronological order come back in exactly that order, and a source rule forbids .sort, .reverse, .toSorted and .toReversed in the picker, because oldest-first is stated in profilesResponseSchema as a promise about muscle memory. THE SWITCH CLAUSE IS ASSERTED STRUCTURALLY: the selected branch must contain await reload() and router.refresh() and must not contain activeProfileId:, so the picker cannot start agreeing with itself while the page shows another profile's rows. THE BADGE IS UNCONDITIONAL: AppShell is rendered with react-dom/server on three different pathnames, with and without a status badge, and profile-badge is present in all three -- no page passes a profile prop, so no route can opt out by forgetting one. FIRST PAINT MAKES NO CLAIM: the badge's first paint is asserted to contain no Choose profile, no Watching as and no href, and the picker's to be aria-busy with Loading profiles and no profile-tile and no no profiles yet -- an empty-household message shown while still asking is the worst thing a picker can say. AVATAR STABILITY IS A PROPERTY, NOT AN EXAMPLE: 500 seeds are asserted to stay in [0,360) and to spread across more than 200 distinct hues, renaming a profile is asserted not to change its hue, and the module is source-scanned for Date., Math.random, process.env, fetch(, globalThis and crypto. with a non-vacuity check. Initials are tested against an astral character and a combining sequence, which displayName[0] would split.

e2e.evidence: EXECUTED Playwright runs at ead34dc, both modes, plus an independent live-server witness. Production, the default: cd e2e && npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium -> 73 tests, 61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed. Development: LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development, same projects -> 73 tests, 70 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. Both counts are IDENTICAL to the round-82 run, which is the point: this task adds a route and a topbar element to a shell every existing spec renders, and the regression evidence is that nothing moved. WHAT THIS GATE DOES NOT COVER, STATED PLAINLY. There is no e2e spec for the profile journey itself, because e2e/** is outside this task's allowedPaths and widening the surface a second time to write one would have been reservation inflation for a file the E2E lane owns. So the executed suite is REGRESSION evidence, not feature evidence, and the feature is evidenced below by a different instrument instead. I recommend a narrow follow-up owning a profiles journey spec; I have not filed it, because PW-0601's certification matrix may already own the row and filing a duplicate is worse than naming the gap here. THE INDEPENDENT WITNESS, which is not a spec reading itself. A real next dev server on 127.0.0.1:3999 was driven with curl against the real handlers and the real in-memory adapter: GET /api/v1/profiles returned outcome listed with 0 profiles and activeProfileId null; POST /api/v1/profiles with the exact three-field strict body returned created with a minted uuid; POST /api/v1/profiles/selection with that id returned selected and the reason selectable_profile_of_account; the next GET returned 1 profile with activeProfileId equal to the minted id. A selection of a well-formed uuid this session does not own returned HTTP 403 with outcome refused and profile_unavailable -- the non-oracle answer -- so the forgeable-scope property holds against the live route and not only in the transport tests. GET /profiles returned 200 and the served bytes contained the escaped heading, Loading profiles and profile-badge-checking, which is the first paint the unit suite asserts, reaching a browser. GET / and GET /search both served profile-badge, so the at all times clause is witnessed on routes this task did not touch. THE DEPLOYMENT BRANCH WAS WITNESSED TOO, on next start against the production build on 127.0.0.1:3998: /profiles served 200 while GET /api/v1/profiles answered HTTP 503 with outcome unavailable and storage_not_configured. That is the honest degraded state the picker is built to render rather than showing an empty household, and it is storage_not_configured rather than authentication_not_configured only because storage is checked first -- the authentication residual PW-0403 owns is behind it, not absent. ONE NARROWING, the same one PL-0704 recorded and it has not changed: the browser under test is NOT the pinned revision. The container ships Chromium 1194 and @playwright/test 1.62.1 requires 1234, so a symlink registry presenting 1194 under the 1234 names was built in a scratch directory and selected with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH; nothing in the repository changed for it. The first attempt this round failed with Executable does not exist because the 1194 tree lays its binary out as chrome-linux/headless_shell while 1.62.1 expects chrome-headless-shell-linux64/chrome-headless-shell -- the registry now maps that layout explicitly, which is worth recording because the previous round's registry would silently stop working after any browser bump. Only api and chromium ran, so this says nothing about WebKit, Firefox or mobile-safari, and no claim is made that the CI job will be green.

recommended.title: Production user authentication, so an account identity is not a typed header
recommended.acceptance: An account identity comes from an authenticated session, not from a header a caller typed. THE RESIDUAL THIS OWNS, IN gpt-architect's OWN WORDS FROM THE PW-0402 VERDICT: "PW-0402 does NOT establish production user authentication. The current account identity still derives from the development-header seam in non-deployment runtime. Keep that residual visible and resolve it before production-sensitive desktop routes are considered authenticated." This task is where that resolves, and until it is DONE no route may be described as authenticated. WHY IT IS P0 AND NOT A TIDY-UP. Every authorization decision in this product is built on the account identity, and PW-0402 proved the decision layer above it is sound -- which makes the identity itself the load-bearing weakness rather than one of several. On a hosted deployment the exposure is nil, because resolveRequestAccount refuses outright with authentication_not_configured. On the DESKTOP it is not: the sidecar runs on the user's machine, the runtime may classify as non-deployment, and every process on that machine can reach the loopback port. PW-0101's launch token stops an unrelated process reaching the LISTENER; it is deliberately incapable of saying who the caller is, and PW-0402 made that incapacity structural. REQUIRED: a real session provider behind resolveRequestAccount, with sessions in PostgreSQL through the Drizzle adapter, per ADR-007 -- which is still recorded as *Proposed* and whose own text says nothing below it may be cited as settled until its governing task's gates pass. PL-0405 is now DONE, so that blocker is gone and ADR-007 should be moved to Accepted in the same change, or the reason it cannot be must be stated. REQUIRED: the development-header path is not deleted -- it is the thing that makes local development possible -- but it must be UNREACHABLE from a build that ships, by the same class of mechanism NonDeploymentEnvironment already uses, and a test must prove a desktop-shaped runtime cannot obtain an identity from it. THAT IS THE SHARPEST CLAUSE IN THIS TASK: today a desktop build classifying as non-deployment would make the header the identity layer, and nothing currently prevents that classification. REQUIRED: the exact Better Auth version is pinned exactly, on the rule this repository applies to Shaka, Playwright and Tauri; ADR-007 pinned 1.7.1 and the reviewer recorded that upstream had moved to 1.7.4, so the pin is reconciled against the version actually reviewed and the hand-written migration is checked against THAT version's schema before anything is generated. REQUIRED: a refusal on an unauthenticated request must not become an oracle, and must compose with PW-0402's route decision rather than adding a second one -- authorizeRoute already returns `unauthenticated` and that stays the single answer. NOT IN SCOPE: authorization, which PW-0402 owns and which the audit found already enforced; the listener boundary, which is PW-0101's; and any identity provider requiring a commercial account or credentials the commander has not supplied -- if one is needed, that is a LAST_MILE item, not a reason to ship a weaker seam.
recommended.notes: Filed round 83 in answer to gpt-architect's request for explicit ownership of the production-authentication gap. No existing task owned it: PW-0402's own approved acceptance is authorization and its verdict names this as a residual; PW-0401 authenticates the desktop forwarder's COUNTERPARTY, which is a different service and a different caller; PW-0101 is the listener and the ruling forbids broadening it. Depends on PW-0402 because the route decision it must compose with has to exist and be reviewed first; that is a genuine build relationship and not the read relationship PW-0402's own edge on PW-0101 turned out to be. Surface includes docs/DECISIONS.md because ADR-007 is still Proposed and PL-0405, the task that blocked its promotion, is DONE.

recommended.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
recommended.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.
